sa_market_summary: The Toyota Hilux is the best-selling vehicle in South Africa and arguably the most iconic bakkie on the continent. Its reputation for indestructibility is well earned ,  it is the go-to workhorse for farmers, contractors, and families. Resale value is outstanding and demand vastly outstrips supply for well-maintained examples. The 2.8 GD-6 engine introduced in 2016 is one of the most capable and reliable diesel engines in the bakkie segment. Parts are universally available across SA.

known_faults.fault: EGR valve and DPF soot buildup (GD-6 diesel)
known_faults.description: The GD-6 diesel engine's EGR valve and DPF can clog, particularly on vehicles used mainly for short city trips where the DPF cannot complete a regeneration cycle. Symptoms include black smoke, power loss, and a DPF warning light.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Ask about primary use case ,  frequent highway driving clears the DPF naturally. Check for DPF warning light. Request DPF cleaning history if above 80,000km of urban use.
known_faults.source: Toyota SA dealer reports, Bakkie owners forums, AutoTrader SA buyer guides

known_faults.fault: Cracked front leaf spring (rough terrain use)
known_faults.description: Hiluxes used heavily off-road or for heavy load carrying can develop cracked front leaf springs. Common on farm and construction vehicles. Can affect steering geometry.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Physically inspect leaf springs for cracks or sagging. Check if the bakkie sits level. Ask about payload and off-road history.
known_faults.source: SA 4x4 community reports, Toyota SA workshop data

known_faults.description: The variable geometry turbocharger actuator on the 2.8 GD-6 can fail or stick, causing power reduction or limp mode. Particularly common in dusty environments (Gauteng, North West).
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Test full throttle acceleration ,  any hesitation or flat spots indicate potential turbo actuator issues. Check for a limp mode history in service records.
known_faults.source: Toyota technical bulletins, SA Hilux owners community

known_faults.description: Fuel injector copper washers can weep diesel at high mileage, causing a slight diesel smell and minor oil contamination. Not catastrophic but should be addressed.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check around injectors for sooty residue or oily buildup. A diesel smell from the engine bay is a tell.
known_faults.source: Toyota SA workshop bulletins, SA diesel specialist reports

what_to_inspect_before_buying: Check the DPF warning light and request DPF cleaning history if the bakkie has done mostly city driving
Inspect leaf springs for cracks or uneven ride height
Confirm the GD-6 turbo is responsive under full acceleration
Check service history ,  Toyota stamp is important for warranty claims
Inspect underbody and chassis for rust (coastal vehicles and farm bakkies)
Test the 4WD system if applicable ,  engage high and low range
Check for any tow bar modification ,  wiring and structural integrity
Confirm the vehicle is not a former fleet or rental unit (high cycle use)
owner_sentiment: Overwhelmingly positive. Hilux owners are among the most loyal in the SA market. Farmers and contractors trust it with their livelihoods. Main complaints are the increasingly complex diesel electronics on GD-6 models compared to older 3.0 D-4D engines. Running costs remain reasonable. Long-distance reliability is excellent.
